newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC Pacific seen seeking US$1 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pacific seen seeking US$1 bln loan.

text.p: Citic Pacific is considering a US$1.0 billion short-term loan for use as bridge financing, bankers said on Friday.
While no formal mandate has been announced, bankers said five banks -- Hongkong Bank, Hang Seng Bank, Chase Asia, J.P. Morgan and BNP -- are tipped to arrange a deal for CITIC.

The loan is expected to have a tenor of between six months and one year, bankers said. They said the loan is likely to be completed as a club deal among a few relationship banks rather than through a general syndication.
CITIC Pacific on Tuesday said it would buy 497.66 million new shares, or 20 percent of China Light & Power Co Ltd's enlarged share capital, at HK$32.66 per share.
CITIC said on Tuesday it would fund the HK$16.25 billion purchase with internal resources and bank borrowings.
Hong Kong bankers said that since CITIC Pacific announced its intention to purchase China Light shares, CITIC has been inundated with offers from banks to arrange financing.
The five banks tipped as arrangers of the rumourd bridge loan either declined comment or could not be reached.
CITIC Pacific also was unavailable for comment.
